Feature flags: turn features on for a share of end users in production or in test, fix them for
testers, and see why someone gets what.

Who gets a flag is set per environment and read top to bottom: switched off, it is off for everyone
there; then an end user's override decides; then the rules, in order; then the share everyone else
gets. Test, which apps using a test key read, follows production until something is changed in it.

Usage:
  voidhash flag <command> [flags]

Aliases:
  flag, flags

Commands:
  list         List the project's feature flags.
  view         Show a flag: its variants, and who gets it in production and in test.
  create       Create a feature flag, off until you turn it on.
  enable       Turn a flag on, optionally for a share of end users.
  disable      Turn a flag off for everyone in an environment.
  rollout      Set the share of end users who get a flag.
  edit         Change a flag's key or description.
  variants     The values a string, number or json flag hands out.
  override     Fix a flag for one end user, whatever its rules say.
  rule, rules  Rules: what share of the end users they match get the flag.
  follow       Make a flag's test follow production again.
  promote      Apply a flag's test configuration to production.
  evaluate     Show what one end user gets from each flag, and why.
  archive      Archive a flag you no longer use.
  restore      Bring back an archived flag as it was.

Flags:
  -h, --help  Show help for this command

Global flags:
  -d, --debug              Print each request and full error detail to standard error
      --no-color           Print without colors (also when NO_COLOR is set)
      --profile <profile>  Use a named config profile: its settings override the base config
                           (default: VOIDHASH_PROFILE)

Run 'voidhash flag <command> --help' for more about a command.
